claim: At grant, US4539507A lists inventors Steven A. VanSlyke and Ching W. Tang and is assigned to Eastman Kodak Company, documenting corporate industrial R&D ownership of an improved thin-film organic electroluminescent device.
metric_value: Eastman Kodak assignee; Tang & VanSlyke inventorship
notes: Origin / ownership facts from the patent document. Not a commercial value amount and not an exact marketed-display mapping.

claim: US4356429A (Tang; Eastman Kodak; granted 1982-10-26) discloses an organic electroluminescent cell with a porphyrinic hole-injecting zone between the anode and luminescent zone, establishing a pre-T0 Kodak organic-EL platform precursor referenced by the later improved-efficiency patent family.
metric_value: organic EL cell with porphyrinic hole-injecting zone (Kodak / Tang 1982)
notes: Pre-T0 family/platform context supporting technical continuity. Not E3 product mapping and not patent-level attributable value for US4539507.

claim: Tang & VanSlyke (Appl. Phys. Lett. 51, 913–915, 1987-09-21) report a bilayer organic thin-film electroluminescent diode with ITO anode and Mg:Ag cathode achieving high external quantum efficiency (~1% photon/electron), luminous efficiency (~1.5 lm/W), and brightness >1000 cd/m² at driving voltage below 10 V — a public lab-device performance signal for a future low-voltage display/emissive platform.
value_carrier: aspirational low-voltage organic EL display / emissive platform (not a marketed product at T0)
metric_value: bilayer organic EL diode >1000 cd/m2 below 10 V with ~1% EQE / ~1.5 lm/W
notes: Package B option/future-value signal observable a decade before Pioneer commercial OLED (1997). Must not be read as R3 implementation in a marketed display at T0=1987-09-21.

claim: The granted patent claims thin-film organic electroluminescent devices with hole-injecting and organic luminescent zones, power conversion efficiency of at least 9×10⁻⁵ w/w, combined active-zone thickness ≤ about 1 micron, and low driving-voltage operation suitable for economical drive circuitry (≤25 V framing in the specification).
value_carrier: claimed thin-film organic EL device modality (patent text; no marketed carrier confirmed at T0)
metric_value: improved-efficiency thin-film organic EL with hole-injecting + luminescent zones
notes: Claimed/described device performance supports option-horizon interpretation for future displays/emitters. Not proof that any marketed OLED product embodied this exact patent at T0.
